transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-05-02
- Time: 09:30 - 10:30 UTC
- Duration: ~60 minutes
- Attendees: Priya, Ethan, Maya, Leo, Samir, Olga

Summary:
Quick triage ahead of hyperscaler pilot flip and feature-flagged rollout. Focus areas: canary plan, feature flag gating logic, KV cache warm-start, SLO/alert thresholds, rollback/playbook readiness. Lots of cross-team dependencies.

Topics:
- Canary plan and perf acceptance criteria
- Feature flag semantics (percentage vs target users vs traffic routing)
- KV cache cold-start and warm-up strategies
- Runbook updates and escalation paths
- QA checks and release gating

Transcript body:
[00:00] Priya Nair: okay everyone thanks for joining on short notice, uh this is the prelaunch triage for the hyperscaler pilot flip, um we've got about an hour, let's go through the checklist and surface any blockers.
[00:18] Ethan Brooks: yep, quick intro from infra side — we're planning to flip 25% traffic in eu-west-1 first, run for 48 hours, then expand. The canary configs are in the canary-run spreadsheet, link is in the meeting notes.
[00:33] Maya Chen: sounds good, quick note — our last sim showed KV cache miss spike on model warm-starts when sequence length varied more than expected, could cause token latency p95 blips.
[00:50] Samir Gupta: hmm okay, that's the prefix-KV cache correct? Is that the one where we saw eviction thrash?
[00:58] Maya Chen: yeah sort of, it's the prefix and the per-shard KV pool, eviction rates shot up when the request mix had a large tail of long contexts — the batching heuristics mispredicted.
[01:12] Priya Nair: to be explicit, is this a hard blocker for flip or a mitigation we can monitor?
[01:20] Ethan Brooks: it's mitigatable — we can do a staged warm-up: seed KV with representative prompts then throttle initial traffic. Also can increase per-GPU KV allocation for the canary. But it will cost more, so we need sign-off.
[01:36] Leo Park: cost vs risk conversation — for pilot we prefer safety. Leo: recommend we accept a temporary cost bump for the first 48 hours to avoid user impact.
[01:46] Olga Ivanov: from QA, we need explicit tests: 1) cold start latency with 0 prefix cache, 2) warm start after seeding, 3) fallback to smaller quantized model variant. I can run those overnight if we lock down test vectors.
[02:05] Samir Gupta: about feature flags — current implementation supports percentage rollouts and user-targeted rollouts, but not traffic-route-based flags. If we need to route by region to the hyperscaler only, we have to add an attribute in the SDK header or do gateway routing.
[02:24] Ethan Brooks: gateway routing would be easier operationally but is heavier because infra needs to maintain the mapping. SDK header approach is quicker to reason about for experiments.
[02:35] Priya Nair: pragmatic approach: for this pilot we do gateway-level traffic rule for eu-west-1 and keep SDK header as follow-up. That way we avoid pushing client changes mid-flip.
[02:47] Maya Chen: agreed. Also add a monitor for model fallback counts — if model variant fallback > 1% for 15m we auto-rollback.
[02:58] Priya Nair: makes sense — define the exact condition later, add to action items.
[03:10] [00:03:10] Ethan Brooks: on SLOs — we propose to set canary SLOs slightly looser, p95 latency target 250ms for generation-only endpoints, error rate < 0.2%. Those are looser than normal but acceptable for early pilot.
[03:28] Leo Park: add SLO for cold-start spike — if p99 increases by >40% vs baseline then page oncall.
[03:36] Maya Chen: oncall — who's owning monitoring during the first 48 hours? Samir?
[03:42] Samir Gupta: I can be primary daytime, Maya backup, and Ethan will be on-call for infra escalations. I'll update the on-call rota doc.
[03:52] Olga Ivanov: QA question — do we have smoke tests that hit fallback/quantized path? I remember some of the older smoke regexes didn't exercise the fallback because of input length distribution.
[04:08] Samir Gupta: right, I updated the smoke harness but haven't pushed it to prod. I'll push a patch after this meeting.
[04:16] Priya Nair: ok put that as action item.
[04:22] [00:04:22] Ethan Brooks: another technical thing — kernel selection for longer contexts; one of the runtime kernels is faster for seq len < 512, another picks up beyond that. We need the canary to reflect the real seq length distribution; otherwise perf numbers will be misleading.
[04:40] Maya Chen: exactly — the canary traffic generator should sample from production histograms, not uniform. I can export histograms by noon.
[04:48] Priya Nair: good.
[04:52] [00:04:52] Leo Park: rollback playbook — two options: soft rollback (shift traffic back to baseline model variant) or hard rollback (flip feature flag off). Soft gives us more time to debug, but hard rollback is quicker and more predictable. Thoughts?
[05:08] Ethan Brooks: start with soft rollback as first action then escalate to hard if errors continue. Automate soft rollback path so it can be triggered by alerts.
[05:18] Olivia: (inaudible)
[05:20] Priya Nair: note — automate via runbook: alert triggers automation to shift 50% traffic back, then pause and escalate. We'll draft the exact runbook steps.
[05:34] [00:05:34] Olga Ivanov: on security/compliance — hyperscaler pilot will process customer data in a new region; confirm that data residency and KMS keys are correct. We need to ensure audit logs flow to the central retention bucket.
[05:50] Samir Gupta: KMS keys are region-scoped; we've created a key in eu-west-1 and hooked it into the private deployment config. Audit logs are currently set to ship but retention policy on the new bucket needs to be updated to 1 year. I'll update ACLs.
[06:06] Maya Chen: also ensure we have SAML SSO test user that can hit the region just in case.
[06:12] Priya Nair: good call.
[06:18] [00:06:18] Ethan Brooks: performance acceptance — what's the minimum we accept to continue expansion? Proposal: after 48 hours, p95 within 15% of baseline and error rate not exceeding 0.3%. If we fail, we pause and investigate.
[06:35] Leo Park: sounds reasonable. Add vendor (competitor) noise: if we see better tail from LambdaScale, do we consider routing to them? that's a separate convo.
[06:48] Priya Nair: let's not gate the pilot on that. We note CloudServeAI and LambdaScale as background.
[06:55] [00:06:55] Samir Gupta: QA gating checklist — I'll list tests that must pass: unit smoke, canary smoke, kv-warmup, fallback trigger, feature-flag gating logic, SDK compatibility. Olga, can you run kv-warmup tests?
[07:07] Olga Ivanov: yes, can start tonight. Expect results by 2026-05-04 morning.
[07:14] Priya Nair: timeline recap — flip 25% on 2026-05-06, run 48 hours, decision point 2026-05-08 09:00 UTC. Is that everyone's understanding?
[07:25] Ethan Brooks: yes, but we need the canary config and seeded KV by 2026-05-05 EOD.
[07:33] Maya Chen: and chaos tests by 2026-05-06 morning.
[07:37] [00:07:37] Leo Park: small note on observability — add a synthetic tracer that measures end-to-end token time including gateway and client side. There's sometimes skew in our token accounting.
[07:50] Samir Gupta: I'll add a synthetic that posts fixed prompts every 30s from a dedicated runner.
[07:57] Priya Nair: thanks.
[08:01] [00:08:01] Ethan Brooks: question — do we want to expose preview logs to hyperscaler SREs or keep logs internal?
[08:12] Maya Chen: for pilot, keep logs internal, but share aggregated metrics. No direct access to raw logs until legal signs off.
[08:20] Olga Ivanov: legal needs to approve retention and PII transfer. I can ping legal.
[08:26] Priya Nair: add legal sign-off as a gating item.
[08:30] [00:08:30] Samir Gupta: quick UX note — feature flag config in console should show rollout percent and region mapping in the same view. I'll file a small UX tweak ticket.
[08:40] Priya Nair: good.
[08:43] [00:08:43] Leo Park: rng random — we should make the feature flag determinism consistent across SDK languages to avoid split-brain allocations. That is, ensure the hash algorithm is stable.
[08:55] Samir Gupta: agreed — I'll add tests for deterministic hashing across go/python/node SDKs.
[09:02] Olga Ivanov: small transcription glitch — sorry.
[09:05] Priya Nair: near the end — any outstanding risks that would block?
[09:10] Ethan Brooks: risk list: KV eviction under long-tail seqs (mitigatable), missing canary traffic distribution (actionable), legal sign-off on logs (blocking), SDK header not ready (we're avoiding it for this pilot).
[09:26] Maya Chen: add one more: quantized fallback path needs more QA. If fallback triggers too often we could see quality regressions.
[09:35] Priya Nair: ok capture that.
[09:38] [00:09:38] Action recap by Priya:
- Priya will publish prelaunch checklist & sign-off matrix (due 2026-05-04)
- Ethan will run canary and seed KV (due 2026-05-05)
- Maya will run contest-style chaos/kv tests (due 2026-05-06)
- Olga will run QA smoke tests (due 2026-05-04)
- Samir will push SDK/console small patches and observability synthetic (due 2026-05-05)
- Leo will finalize runbook & on-call rota (due 2026-05-03)

[00:10:15] Priya Nair: thanks all, we'll reconvene if any major blocker surfaces before the flip, otherwise decision point meeting on 2026-05-08 at 09:00 UTC. I'll send calendar invite and the consolidated checklist.

End of transcript.
